newsitem.title: UK: More airline slots needed, not auctions - IATA.
newsitem.headline: More airline slots needed, not auctions - IATA.

text.p: An auction of airline slots will increase costs rather than competition, International Air Transport Association (IATA) director-general Pierre Jeanniot said on Monday.

"We are dealing with a European world where there is talk of slot auctions, which will increase the costs, rather than concentrate on providing more slots which would increase competition," he told a conference on the future of air transport industry.
"And a European world where absurd and archaic national policies still pretend to justify maintaining national borders in the sky when they have been dismantled on the ground."
Jeanniot said he was looking to next February's meeting of transport ministers meeting within the European Civil Aviation Conference (ECAC) to introduce a business-like structure.

This should, "deliver significant improvements, centralise on a European-wide basis regulatory oversight and route structure planning, while separating it from the delivery of air traffic control services," he added.
Reviewing the European aviation market which should be fully integrated, at least for EU countries in 1997, Jeanniot said:

"An integrated "open sky market" in Europe could be treated like the North American market and relations between these markets could clearly benefit by a blurring of distinction between fifth freedom and cabotage."

Fifth freedom rights allow airlines on arrival in a country to pick up passengers or cargo for a destination in a third country. Cabotage permits an airline from one country being able to carry traffic within another country.

"In other words, a true "open skies" deal would entail the ability of all US, Canadian and Mexican carriers to operate to and from any points in Europe, as well as the ability to operate within any European country," Jeanniot added.
"Similarly European carriers would be free to operate to and from any points in North America and between those three North American countries," he said

"Anything less than that is not "open skies". If that sounds like utopia, then we still have far to go to achieve true multilaterism," Jeanniot said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
